description: IGNIX is a multidisciplinary team competing in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We're building an AI-powered dashboard that transforms microgravity combustion research into clear, actionable fire-safety insights for human space exploration. We combine AI, data analysis, software development, and scientific curiosity to turn complex NASA research into meaningful insights. Our goal: safer missions through smarter data.
summary:
FIRENEX turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into an evidence explorer for spacecraft cabin fire safety, organised as Prevention, Detection and Suppression. Test-based answers come only from real NASA test rows. Where the data has no matching test, FIRENEX says "NO TEST DATA" instead of guessing, and simulations and model outputs are clearly labelled.

It addresses the challenge by making evidence gaps visible. In the PSI data we used, solid-material tests stop at 22.2% O₂, yet lunar cabins are planned at 34% O₂ / 8.2 psia. The ISS smoke detector's obscuration channel also barely responded to Kapton and Teflon smoke (median drop 0.001 V vs 0.30 V for Silicone). FIRENEX includes a Cabin Check, an Evidence Gap Radar, a Detection Panel built on the ISS detector's own recordings, a Suppression View (63 of 78 matched FLEX flames went out at cabin conditions), a labelled Flame Lab simulation, and a Safe Predictor that refuses to answer outside its tested data.

It matters because fire-safety decisions for future habitats need evidence, and knowing exactly where evidence is missing is as valuable as having it.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Lunar cabins are planned around 34% O₂ / 8.2 psia, but NASA's PSI data has no solid-material test rows above 22.2% O₂. The ISS smoke detector also barely responds to some smoke (median 0.001 V for Kapton and Teflon vs 0.30 V for Silicone). Fire-safety decisions need evidence, and in these cases the evidence has gaps.

WHAT WE BUILT

FIRENEX is a web dashboard that works only from real NASA test rows. It is organised as Prevention, Detection and Suppression:

- Cabin Check: pick a material, oxygen level and pressure. The verdict comes from matched PSI test rows, with the rows shown. If nothing matches, the answer is NO TEST DATA (for example PMMA at 34% O₂).

- Inventory Screener: checks a whole cabin material list against ISS, Moon and spacesuit atmospheres.

- Evidence Gap Radar: shows where NASA's tests cluster and where there are none.

- Detection Panel: replays the ISS smoke detector's own recordings (SAME-R, 68,699 readings).

- Flame Lab: Earth vs microgravity flame simulation, clearly labelled as simulated, driven by measured PSI-108 spread rates.

- Suppression View: 63 of 78 matched real FLEX flames went out at cabin conditions (21% O₂ / 14.7 psia).

- Safe Predictor: a scikit-learn decision tree trained on 273 FLEX droplet tests (74.5% holdout accuracy vs 67.3% baseline). It refuses to predict outside the tested envelope.

- Investigation Cards and Ask Flame: browse all 19 PSI investigations and search the evidence, with sources.

HONESTY BY DESIGN

Every displayed number traces to a NASA source file, and simulations are labelled. Limits are stated in the app (only 546 of 2,012 records record an outcome; the predictor's margin is modest). Before submission, every number was recomputed from the source files and the tools were tested with edge cases (see BUILD-REPORT.md in the repository).

TECH

Static web app (HTML/CSS/JavaScript, GSAP), data pipeline in Python, model trained with scikit-learn and exported to JSON so it runs fully in the browser.

LINKS
